notable.title: Ending Birth Tourism
notable.summary: The U.S. stops people from visiting just to have babies here and get citizenship. New rules will block these trips and punish those who help.

notable.title: Continuing To Protect the Meaning and Value of American Citizenship
notable.summary: It changes rules so U.S. papers won't prove citizenship for kids whose parents are certain foreign workers, terrorists, or who paid to be born here. The government will stop giving or accepting those papers.

notable.title: National Purple Heart Day, 2026
notable.summary: Declares August 7, 2026, as National Purple Heart Day and asks Americans to thank wounded and fallen soldiers.

notable.title: Adjusting Imports of Polysilicon and Its Derivatives Into the United States
notable.summary: It limits foreign polysilicon coming into the U.S. to protect national security and help domestic makers.

notable.title: Continuation of U.S. Drug Interdiction Assistance to the Government of Colombia
notable.summary: The president allows U.S. forces to stop planes in Colombia if they look like they are carrying illegal drugs, but only after trying to warn them first.

notable.title: Establishing the President's Military Spouse Commission
notable.summary: A new group is created to help military spouses by advising the President on policies that improve their lives. It brings together spouses of top military and government leaders to share ideas.

notable.title: Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Advancement by Countries of ...
notable.summary: Extends a national emergency for one more year to stop certain countries from using U.S. investments to build up military and cyber weapons.

notable.title: To Facilitate Positive Adjustment to Competition From Imports of Quartz Surface Products
notable.summary: The President allows extra time for U.S. companies to adjust as more quartz countertops are imported. It targets countries not covered by free trade deals.

notable.title: Authorizing Cameron County, Texas, To Own, Operate, and Maintain the Brownsville and ...
notable.summary: The US now lets Cameron County, Texas, own and run the Brownsville-Matamoros Bridge. The county must keep it safe, follow all laws, and get permission before selling or transferring it.

notable.title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 101 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 ...
notable.summary: The president lets the Commerce Department control supplies of certain recycled minerals needed for national defense. This helps ensure the U.S. has enough materials to stay safe.

notable.title: Substances Generally Recognized as Safe
notable.summary: Starting now, companies must ask the FDA for permission before adding new food ingredients. The agency wants to review safety claims to protect people and animals.

notable.title: HUD's Implementation of the Fair Housing Act's Disparate Impact Standard; Amendments to ...
notable.summary: Removes rules making housing programs legally responsible for unfair effects, even without proof of intentional bias. Reopens public comments until October 9, 2026.

notable.title: Accessible Lavatories on Single-Aisle Aircraft and Ensuring Safe Accommodations for Air ...
notable.summary: Enforcement of some airline wheelchair rules is delayed until April 2027 so officials can study public feedback before deciding on final changes.

notable.title: NRC Modernization: Rulemaking Procedure, Federal Advisory Committee Act Alignment ...
notable.summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission updates its rules to make procedures clearer, match federal advisory standards, and improve security requirements. It also sets a deadline for public feedback before the changes take effect.

notable.title: Reforms to 13 CFR 124.103 To Remove SBA's 8(a) Program's Rebuttable Presumption of Social ...
notable.summary: The government changes a rule so people must prove they faced unfair treatment themselves to join a small business program, instead of just being assumed eligible because of their race. It does not change anything for businesses owned by groups.
